title: Slice pullback comparison is induced by the ringed localization square
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a continuous functor defining a morphism $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ whose inverse image preserves finite limits, and let $R$ on $\mathcal D$ and $S$ on $\mathcal C$ be sheaves of commutative rings with a ring map $c:f^{-1}R\to S$. For $V\in\mathcal D$ put $U=u(V)$, give $\mathcal D/V$ and $\mathcal C/U$ the localized topologies and restricted rings [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and let $f_V$, the commutative ringed localization square and the ordinary module comparison $\sigma:(f_V)^*j_V^*\cong j_U^*f^*$ be those of [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. Use the unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with localization functor $q$, the exact derived restrictions $j_V^*,j_U^*$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction], the derived pullbacks $Lf^*,Lf_V^*$ computed on K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], and the derived adjunctions $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Lf_V^*\dashv R(f_V)_*$. Let $\beta:j_V^*Rf_*\cong R(f_V)_*j_U^*$ and $\theta:Lf_V^*j_V^*\cong j_U^*Lf^*$ be the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization]. Then for every K-flat complex $P$ of $R$-modules with flat terms, under the identifications $Lf^*(qP)\cong q(f^*P)$ and $Lf_V^*(q\,j_V^*P)\cong q((f_V)^*j_V^*P)$ (the restriction $j_V^*P$ is again K-flat with flat terms) and the termwise identifications $j_V^*(qP)=q(j_V^*P)$, $j_U^*(q f^*P)=q(j_U^*f^*P)$, the component $\theta_{qP}$ equals $q(\sigma_P)$. Consequently $\theta$ is the derived pullback comparison induced by the commutative ringed localization square, and $\beta$ is its exchange mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], that is, the base change map of this square.

proof.text: Write $F=f^*,G=f_*,F_v=(f_V)^*,G_v=(f_V)_*$ on complexes, $r=j_V^*,s=j_U^*$, and $L=Lf^*,R=Rf_*,L_v=Lf_V^*,R_v=R(f_V)_*$. Composition $a;b$ is in order. The localized ringed morphism and sectionwise-identity map $\tau:rG\to G_vs$ come from [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-slice-module-pullback-isIso], $\mathsf T'_0(\sigma_P)=r(\eta^0_P);\tau_{FP}$; naturality with the differentials gives the same identity for chain maps.

Take the global and local normalized presentations of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-image-exists], writing $\alpha:Lq\to qF,\iota:qG\to Rq$ and $\alpha',\iota'$ locally. Let $\rho:rq\cong qr$, $\zeta:sq\cong qs$ be [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. The right augmentation square required by the new transpose lemma is exactly [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-comparisons]; its derived unit square is the unit compatibility of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization], with $\theta$ oriented $L_vr\to sL$. Explicitly, normalization is $\mathsf T_D(\alpha_A;qh)=q(\mathsf T_0(h));\iota_I$ and likewise locally. The right square is $r(\iota_I);\beta_{qI};R_v(\zeta_I)=\rho_{GI};q(\tau_I);\iota'_{sI}$. Compose the unit compatibility with $R_v(\theta)$ and cancel $\theta^{-1}$ to obtain $\eta'^D_{rqA};R_v(\theta_{qA})=r(\eta^D_{qA});\beta_{LqA}$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $j_V$ with identity ring map: $rP$ is K-flat with flat terms. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], $\alpha_P$ and $\alpha'_{rP}$ are isomorphisms. These give exactly the model identifications in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat): pullback along a morphism of ringed topoi keeps K-flat complexes with flat terms K-flat with flat terms, applied to the localization morphism j_V of sites-modules.tex Tag 04J0 (lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites), whose module pullback is restriction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalized-adjunction-square-transpose] to Step 2's presentations at $P$. It gives $\mathsf T'_D(\theta_{qP};s(\alpha_P);\zeta_{FP})=\rho_P;q(r(\eta^0_P);\tau_{FP});\iota'_{sFP}$. By local Hom normalization [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-image-exists], Step 1, and naturality of the Hom bijection in its source, this also equals $\mathsf T'_D(L_v(\rho_P);\alpha'_{rP};q(\sigma_P))$. Injectivity gives equality of the two maps; cancellation of Step 3's isomorphisms proves $\theta_{qP}=q(\sigma_P)$ under the specified identifications.

proof.text: Choose $p:P\to A$ flat-term K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Since $qp$ is invertible, naturality forces $\theta_{qA}=L_vr(qp)^{-1};\theta_{qP};sL(qp)$, proving determination and resolution independence. The counit compatibility of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization] is $L_v(\beta_M);\varepsilon'_{sM}=\theta_{RM};s(\varepsilon_M)$. Thus [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] identifies $\beta$ as the transpose of the right side, precisely the base change map of Stacks 07A7 for the ringed square of Step 1.
